asset: fresh disposable SPL test token, 6 decimals; no real USDC or real SOL
mechanism: Client-only and fully signed representations co-sign to identical wire bytes. Baseline reservations use different signer identities; patched reservations use the primary signature from post-cosign bytes.
findings: Concurrent Devnet baseline: one ledger transfer, two successful HTTP responses and paid-handler invocations.
Concurrent patched: one ledger transfer, one successful response, one signature_consumed rejection before a second RPC submission.
Sequential baseline: second submission blocked by real Devnet preflight AlreadyProcessed; adapter reports send_failed. Patched rejects earlier as signature_consumed.
limits: One concurrent pair per variant observed; scheduling and public RPC behavior can vary.
Replay markers remain process-local; restart/multi-instance persistence is not supplied by this patch.
Explorer screenshots establish ledger facts; local HTTP logs establish handler access. Neither alone proves both.
Offline HTTP logs use simulated RPC and are separately labeled.

The fully signed representation was deliberately prepared with the disposable operator key. This tests replay handling when both valid representations are available; it does not establish that an untrusted client can obtain the operator-signed form before the first submission or confirmation.

The original harness reported boot preflight enabled, but did not capture PAY_KIT_DISABLE_PREFLIGHT. Boot preflight is not independently established by that flag; transaction preflight is established by the recorded skipPreflight=false RPC options. The reproduction script now clears the inherited override.
private_keys: Stored outside repository and excluded from all evidence.
